items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 15:229:1
items.html: In the days of Purim one gives to whoever stretches out his hand, etc. For the discernment of the Malchut of the second restriction is called a lock, as above, in the secret of the verse “passing upon the handles of the lock.” For it locks upon the lights, so that they should not expand from her downward, in order that the externals should not take hold in them; for as long as the lights are lacking GAR there is in them a grip for the externals, as above in the previous parts. However, at the time when the Yesod of Aba clothes in her, which is the secret of “passing upon the handles of the lock,” since it is in the secret of long, that is, GAR, there is no grip whatsoever for the externals in this great light, and therefore one gives to whoever stretches out his hand.
